sections.h2: Who records deeds in Clay County, Missouri?
sections.html:
The Clay County Recorder of Deeds, Sandra Brock, records deeds, deeds of trust, plats, surveys, powers of attorney and tax liens for the county. The office sits in the Clay County Administration building at 1 Courthouse Square in Liberty, with a mailing address of PO Box 238, Liberty, MO 64069. The phone number is 816-407-3550 and the email is recorder@claycountymo.gov.

Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., but the office accepts no recordings or marriage licenses after 4:00 p.m. If you plan to sign a deed late in the afternoon, ask your title company to send it in before that cutoff. The county notes that there is no recorder location at the Annex, so go to the courthouse square address.

Under the county recorder page, the office does not decide which documents must be recorded. Its job is to confirm that what you present meets state format rules, then keep the record permanently. Everything it records is public.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Clay County?
sections.html:
A standard document costs $26.00 for the first page plus $3.00 for each additional page, paid by cash, check or credit card. Cards carry a transaction fee charged by the processor. A statewide fee change took effect on August 28, 2026 and added a flat $2.00 to recording charges, so older fee sheets you may have saved are out of date.

The state side of the charge sits in RSMo 59.319, which lists a six dollar user fee collected on every recorded instrument on top of other fees. Three dollars of that user fee stays with the recorder in a fund for record storage and preservation. For page-by-page pricing on a long document, call the office before you send it.

sections.h2: What format rules can get a deed rejected?
sections.html:
A deed that does not follow the format rules in RSMo 59.310 can be refused, or recorded as a non-standard document for the extra $25.00. The county's document standards page lists the details.

  • White or light paper, 8 1/2 by 11 inches, 20 pound weight, no watermarks or logos, printed on one side only.
  • Type no smaller than 8 point, in black or dark ink, with signatures in dark ink and the signer's name typed or printed underneath.
  • A 3 inch blank top margin on the first page and 3/4 inch margins elsewhere.
  • On page one: the document title, its date, all grantors with marital status, all grantees, any statutory addresses, the full legal description and the reference book and page when one applies.

The county asks for the full legal description and says it should not be taken from tax bills. Documents signed before January 1, 2002, military separation papers, documents signed outside the United States, certified copies and court judgments are exempt from the standardization rules. The office returns any rejected document with the reason written out.

sections.h2: How do I find or copy a recorded deed in Clay County?
sections.html:
Search the county's online records through the iCounty portal at claymo.icounty.com. You register as a user, and viewing images is free, but copies must be purchased. For subscription questions, call iCounty at (816) 295-1540. The recorder's own line, 816-407-3550, handles everything else.

Records are indexed by name, so a search by street address will not work. The office suggests getting a property printout from the Clay County Assessor's real estate division, which shows the book and page of the deed and speeds up a copy request. The office says its online records run from 1968 to the present. Deeds were hand recorded in books from 1822 until an automated database began in 1986, and imaging of daily records started in August 1999.

A copy costs $2.00 for the first page and $1.00 for each added page. A certified copy adds $1.00 per document. Credit card orders can be emailed or mailed.

sections.h2: What can the Clay County recorder not do for a seller?
sections.html:
The recorder cannot search for liens or tell you whether a lien exists, because state statute bars the office from making that determination. Use the public computer at the office, or ask a title company to run the search. The recorder also cannot change a recorded deed. To add or remove a name, a new deed has to be prepared and recorded at the current fee.

  • No sale price lookup: the sales price is not public record in Clay County, and the Assessor may be able to supply market value for the area.
  • No structure information: the recorder's files describe land, so ask the Assessor when improvements were added.
  • No blank forms: the office cannot prepare legal documents, so a quit claim or warranty deed comes from you or an attorney.
  • No foreclosure list: watch the Kearney Courier or the Excelsior Springs Daily Standard for notices, then call the trustee named in the notice.

Paying off a mortgage records a release of the deed of trust. The release is not proof of ownership, since the deed from your seller is the document that shows you own the home. The county also runs Deed Watch, a free email alert at deedwatch.com that tells you when a document is recorded under a name you choose.

sections.h2: What does Clay County look like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Clay County was organized on January 2, 1822 and named for Henry Clay. The county seat is Liberty. The county covers 409 square miles, of which 397 are land, and ranks fifth in Missouri by 2020 population at 253,335. It forms part of the Kansas City metro area, and Clay County holds the northern suburbs plus a piece of Kansas City itself.

The Census Bureau estimated 265,032 residents on July 1, 2025 and 110,443 housing units. Owner-occupied homes make up 69.5% of units, the median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $275,600, and median household income is $88,468. Median gross rent is $1,243 and the mean commute is 22.8 minutes. The county issued 297 building permits in 2025.

Cities and towns include Liberty, Gladstone, Excelsior Springs, Smithville, Kearney, North Kansas City, Pleasant Valley, Claycomo and Missouri City. School districts serving the county are Liberty 53, North Kansas City 74, Kearney R-I, Smithville R-II, Excelsior Springs 40 and the elementary district at Missouri City. Interstates 29, 35 and 435 cross the county, along with US 69, 71 and 169.

Whichever town your home is in, the same Liberty office records the deed. Ask your title company or closing attorney who will deliver it and when, so the new deed is on file before the 4:00 p.m. cutoff.

faqs.q: How much does the Clay County Recorder of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A standard deed costs $26.00 for the first page and $3.00 for each added page. A non-standard document adds $25.00. The charges reflect the statewide $2.00 increase that took effect August 28, 2026. Confirm page counts and card fees with the office at 816-407-3550.

faqs.q: What are the Clay County recorder's hours for filing a deed?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., but it takes no recordings after 4:00 p.m. It is at 1 Courthouse Square in Liberty. The mailing address is PO Box 238, Liberty, MO 64069.

faqs.q: Can I search Clay County deeds by property address?
faqs.a: No. Records are indexed by name, not location. Get the book and page from the Clay County Assessor's real estate division, then use the recorder's online search or call the office. Online viewing is free once you register, while copies are paid.

faqs.q: Can the recorder fix a name or legal description on a deed that is already recorded?
faqs.a: No. A recorded document is a permanent record and cannot be edited. To change the title, a new deed or corrective document has to be prepared by you or an attorney and recorded at the current fee.

faqs.q: Does Clay County charge a transfer tax when a deed is recorded?
faqs.a: The county fee schedule shows recording, copy, certification and marriage license charges and lists no transfer tax line. For any other charge connected to a particular closing, ask the Recorder of Deeds at 816-407-3550 or your title company.
